clue.text: Matches underwear with a lining

indicators.note: the single letter sits inside the garment word as a lining sits inside clothing

parts.note: vests are undergarments worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: Someone coordinates their underclothes with a lined garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' looks like a verb about coordinating clothes, but it is the plural noun for things you strike to light a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestas are a traditional brand-turned-generic name for short wax matches struck to make fire.

clue.text: Closely studies a cathedral city

parts.note: a den is a private study room, so studies gives dens
Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone pores over a cathedral city in close detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things packed tightly together, an adverbial synonym pair.

clue.text: Dieting so can result in efficient use of food

indicators.note: the clue says these letters can be turned into something else, a signal that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Going on a diet is claimed to help the body process its meals well.
explanation.definitionFit: The body breaking down meals to extract nourishment is the process this describes.

clue.text: Sewing material that's right in the modern era

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is placed within the other letters, as in signals

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, labels years of the current era

explanation.surface: A dressmaking supply is said to be the correct one for today.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton strands used with a needle to stitch fabric are the material described.

clue.text: Specimen shown by representative in auction

indicators.note: the representative is placed inside the auction word

parts.note: a sale is an event where goods are sold, as at an auction
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: An example item is displayed by a sales agent at an auction house.
explanation.definitionFit: A small portion taken to show what the whole is like is a specimen.

clue.text: Point to a man of the type to be a fast runner

parts.note: S, south, is one of the compass points
a printer works with type, the metal letters used in printing

explanation.surface: Someone points to a man who looks the sort to run quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who races over short distances at top speed is described.

clue.text: Saw a non drinker in low accommodation

indicators.note: the cattle sound gives accommodation to the abstainer, housing it inside

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a teetotaller staying in humble lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, a guiding saying like a motto.

clue.text: A subject of fifty-one, say, getting call-up

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals
eg, for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: Someone aged fifty-one, perhaps, is being called up for service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call-up' looks like conscription; split it, 'up' turning NAME into EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal bound to serve a lord is a subject owing allegiance.

clue.text: Faculty of fellows rowing about an agreement

indicators.note: the crew word goes around the word of agreement

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A college faculty of rowing fellows debates a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department, but here it is a bodily ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the human senses, and a sense is a faculty.

clue.text: Put down for wren and tit perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the bird names may be arranged otherwise, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A note records sightings of a wren and a tit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put down on paper has been recorded in writing.

clue.text: Discrimination makes sense

definitions.meaning: discernment in matters of style and quality
one of the five senses, the one using the tongue

explanation.surface: Telling good from bad is just common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined judgement in style and the faculty of the palate share one word.

clue.text: A gang — one many would find very wicked

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so it can stand for many

explanation.surface: A gang member is someone many people would think thoroughly evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly depraved and shameless is described as given over to vice.

clue.text: Some would describe this as a gamble

indicators.note: some of the letters of the words describe this make the answer

explanation.surface: Many would call this a risky venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager staked on an uncertain outcome is a gamble.

clue.text: Thrown out, idles in isolation

indicators.note: thrown means the letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ejected, the layabouts find themselves alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone and apart from others is the state described.

clue.text: Charm to wind up the listener

parts.note: to wind up is to end or finish
an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A charmer tries to tease the person listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' looks like teasing someone, but it means finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to win their affection, making them fond of you.

clue.text: Basis for writing 30?

parts.note: a song at 30-across is written out in musical notes, so the paper used for it is a pun on musical notation

explanation.surface: What would one need to compose the song at 30-across?
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery is the basic sheet anyone writes letters on.

clue.text: Repartee is good only in one's youth

parts.words: is good only in one's youth
parts.note: something good only when young is no good when old, which split into words describes this banter

explanation.surface: Witty back-and-forth is said to suit only the young.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into BAD IN AGE: what is good only in youth is bad in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful witty exchange of remarks is banter.

clue.text: A fool who's a little too affectionate

indicators.note: a little of the phrase too affectionate holds the answer

explanation.surface: A fool is someone a bit overly fond.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, stupid person is a lout or idiot.

clue.text: The male figures where support's required

definitions.text: The male figures where support's required

parts.words: The male figures where support's required
parts.note: carved men used as columns hold up a building, named after a Titan who bore the heavens

explanation.surface: Men step in wherever help is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Architectural columns carved as men, plural of a Titan's name, bear loads.

clue.text: Quietly, backing or showing favour

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: backing means the word or is read backwards

explanation.surface: Softly supporting, or showing approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Being for something, in favour of it, is the sense.

clue.text: Overdue set of books hidden

parts.note: late means behind time
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Overdue library books have been hidden away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant and not yet visible is concealed.

clue.text: Change a pound for a friend

parts.note: P, pence, is small change
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone swaps money with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate or chum is a close companion.

clue.text: Common soldier

explanation.surface: An ordinary infantryman.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread and the top army rank are one word.

clue.text: A devotee of the new head cracked

indicators.note: new means the letters of head are made into a new order

parts.note: rent means torn or split apart

explanation.surface: A follower of the new leader has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns HEAD into ADHE; 'head cracked' looks like madness.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause is a devotee.

clue.text: Agitated indeed, though it's not admitted

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flustered insists something is true, while it stays unconfessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something refused or disowned is not acknowledged.

clue.text: Moderate anger

explanation.surface: Keep your rage in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone down and a fit of rage share one word.

clue.text: Really keen saver, clever yet glum

parts.note: a miser hoards money
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: A thrifty, clever person is nonetheless gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappy and dejected describes someone glum.

clue.text: Go off loving upwardly mobile East European

indicators.note: in a down clue, upwardly means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: An ambitious man from Eastern Europe runs off for love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwardly mobile' looks like social climbing but reverses E and POLE as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away secretly with a lover to marry is the act.

clue.text: Set to the side, raising a smile

parts.note: a beam is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone sits sideways, managing a grin.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, something at right angles to the keel lies off the vessel's side.

clue.text: Put an end to restriction being applied

definitions.text: Put an end to restriction being applied

parts.words: Put an end to restriction being applied
parts.note: killing by tightening a cord round the neck is a deadly restriction

explanation.surface: Abolish regulations once enforced.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle with a cord ends life by constriction of the throat.

clue.text: Song composed about a small daughter

indicators.note: the calm word goes about the other letters

parts.note: serene means calm or composed
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A song written about a little girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Music sung beneath a lover's window at evening is this kind of song.

clue.text: Revolting individuals!

parts.note: revolting seems to mean disgusting, but it means rising up against authority

explanation.surface: Some people are disgusting!
explanation.definitionFit: Insurgents rising in revolt against those in power.
